reason: Same meaning as the FLOPO value 'pinnately branched', whose listed bearers already include vascular bundle PO:0005020 (vein). Veins 'pinnately branching' are branches in two rows on either side of a main vein.

target: new: two values of one bearer (punctate PATO_0001512 and striated PATO_0001410)
reason: The lemma surface is both finely dotted and finely striate. Both qualities hold at once, so this is not a continuum between two shapes. It should split into two annotations, not become a compound term.
'Scale-shaped' involucres, bracts and leaves are scale-like: reduced, thin and flat like a scale. FLOPO already has that value.

label: partially mycoheterotrophic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its having chlorophyll and photosynthesising while also obtaining part of its carbon and nutrients from mycorrhizal fungi.
reason: A real nutritional category of green plants, distinct from holomycotrophic (FLOPO:0991374) and autotrophic (FLOPO:0991258), and the source contrasts it explicitly ('plants with chlorophyll, semi-mycotrophic'). It would be a sibling of those two under trophic quality.
The same word as the existing FLOPO value, spelled without the hyphen. Add it as a spelling variant.
Here the prefix 'sub-' means 'nearly': this is an approximate pinnatisect, the same treatment as 'suborbicular'. The bearer 'segment' still needs to be resolved to the organ it belongs to.

A basin is round, wide and shallowly concave, which is the definition of saucer-shaped. The examples are basin-shaped cupules and corolla tubes. Deeper structures would be cup-shaped (PATO_0002227) instead.

'Coadnate' means grown together. In 'stamens coadnate' and 'filaments coadnate', parts of the same kind are fused, which is connate. 'Coadnate to rachis' joins two different parts and should go through pattern 09 with adnate (FLOPO:0991129).
'Style extending up to corolla throat' and 'veins extending up to ...' relate the part to the point it reaches. That is the relational quality 'extends to', with the other part named in the sentence.

Alveolate is defined as having close-set angular depressions like a honeycomb, which fits the seed coats and mericarps. For tertiary veins, 'honeycomblike' describes the vein network, so it would be reticulate (FLOPO:0991100) instead.

All six statements come from one sentence about the cuticular ridges of apical cells, a microstructure that has no PO class. The bearer was mis-grounded to the spadix. With one source and no bearer, no term or rule is justified.

target: corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017), position upper (FLOPO:0991376) via docs/odp/18-position-of-the-bearer.md
reason: This is not a quality word but a measurement of a part. The bearer is the upper corolla lip, and the quality is length (or width) with the measured numbers.

Bract blades, styles and stigmas 'mucro-shaped' are reduced to a short, sharp point. Mucronate (FLOPO:0991054) would be wrong, because it means bearing a mucro rather than being one. 'Pointed' is the closest correct existing term.
'Nonsheathing' leaves and bracts are 'not sheathing', the same treatment as 'unlobed' = not lobed.

'Connective not extended' and 'lateral veins (of the lemma) not extended' mean the part does not run beyond the apex or margin, which is 'not excurrent'. The fruit-margin examples (Spanish/Portuguese) are unclear and should go to review.
'Corymbosely branched' is branched into a corymb-like, flat-topped shape. The prefix 'sub-' makes it an approximate value of corymb-like, so no new term is needed.
PO has only the grass leaf-sheath auricle (PO_0020106), which does not fit petioles or keel petals. Negating PATO auriculate expresses the statement for any of these bearers.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (surface or region of the bearer: abaxial surface) + puberulous (FLOPO:0991049)
reason: The quality is puberulous. 'Abaxially' says which surface of the bearer carries it, which the surface/region pattern handles.
'Marginate' is having a distinct marginal band, which is FLOPO 'margined'. 'Broadly' describes how wide the band is and stays in the record as a qualifier.
This is the continuum between ovate (FLOPO:0991024) and lanceolate (PATO_0001877), as already decided for 'ovate-lanceolate'. 'Broadly' is a width modifier that stays in the record.

label: callose-serrate
definition: A serrated quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's marginal teeth each ending in a small, hard, thickened point (a callosity).
reason: This follows the earlier decision for spinose-serrate (FLOPO:0991256): one serration type whose teeth carry a callus, not two separate qualities of the margin. The tip form matches callus-tipped (FLOPO:0991346).

label: campylodromous
definition: A branched quality inhering in a leaf by virtue of its primary veins, or primary and basal secondary veins, arising at or near a single point and running in strong, recurved arches before converging towards the leaf apex.
reason: This is a standard Hickey venation type that is missing from PATO's set (actinodromous, brochidodromous and others, all under branched PATO:0000402). It is distinct from camptodromous (FLOPO:0991368), which is pinnate. Propose it to PATO alongside the existing venation terms.
'Lenticular' was already mapped to biconvex, and a lens shape is compressed by definition. 'Compressed' only stresses that, so it adds no second value.

A concaulescent peduncle or pedicel is fused to the stem above the axil it arises from, which is adnation to a structure of a different kind. The stem is implied by the word and fills the 'towards' slot.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (surface or region of the bearer: plant organ apex FLOPO_0985023) + low brightness (PATO_0000327)
reason: The quality is a dark colour, located at the tip of the bearer. The region pattern places it on the apex, so no compound term is needed.

target: new: two values of one bearer (non-deciduous PATO_0001732 and fibrous FLOPO:0991026)

label: gradate
definition: An imbricate quality inhering in a set of bracts by virtue of their being in several overlapping series that become progressively shorter from the inner to the outer series.
reason: This is a standard term for Asteraceae involucres and differs from equal or subequal series. Imbricate alone loses the stepwise change in length, so the new class sits under imbricate.

This combines two values: an ovate outline that is narrow by length-to-width ratio, and an asymmetry ('obliquely'). Both exist, so it should not become a compound term.
